---
title: "Permissions, sandboxes, and isolation"
---

An approval prompt is a decision gate; a rule is an instruction or policy; a hook can transform an event; a container or VM is an environment boundary. They solve different problems. An agent denied a native file-read may still reach the same benign file through an allowed shell command, so permission configuration is not an OS sandbox.

Lab 3 demonstrates this distinction only with fake files in a disposable folder. It compares normal approvals with auto mode, command-pattern blocks with equivalent scripts, and an optional separately launched process. Native child sessions may inherit derived restrictions; do not describe them as a security escape.

::: {.callout-important}
Containers limit impact on the host but do not protect data sent to the model provider. Rules and ignore files can be bypassed. Stronger controls combine least privilege, environment isolation, deterministic checks, human review, and recovery.
:::
